title: CLMS Net Primary Production (NPP) Global 300m 10-daily V2 (NetCDF)
description: Defined as the net amount of biomass, or carbon, produced by plants per unit area and time, expressed in gC/m²/day. It is equal to the difference between the Gross Primary Production (GPP), i.e. the total amount of carbon produced through photosynthesis, and the amount of energy used for plant respiration. Every 10-days estimates are available in near real time at global scale in the spatial resolution of about 300 m from January 2014 to the present.

bands.name: qflag
bands.cdse:short_description: Quality Flag of the Net Primary Production
bands.cdse:long_description: The quality flag (QFLAG) summarises, for each pixel, the conditions under which the Net Primary Production value was produced — for instance whether the input fAPAR or meteorological data were missing, whether the pixel is evergreen broadleaf forest, or whether the FAPAR value was corrected for low values, filled from the previous dekad or interpolated — enabling users to filter the dataset according to their quality requirements.

cdse:browser_search_path: CLMS Bio-geophysical Parameters, Vegetation, Net/Gross Primary Production
cdse:collection_description: Net Primary Production (NPP) is defined as the net amount of biomass, or carbon, produced by vegetation per unit area and time (gC/m²/day). NPP is obtained by subtracting from the Gross Primary Production (GPP) — i.e. the total amount of carbon produced through photosynthesis — the amount of energy consumed by plant respiration. Estimates are generated at 10-day intervals at global scale, with a spatial resolution of about 300 m, and the time series extends from January 2014 to the present.
